children: HDFC Bank shares slipped marginally on Friday, trading at ₹682.70 on the NSE by 10.52 am, down 0.09 per cent from the previous close of ₹683.30. The stock opened flat at ₹683.30, touched an intraday high of ₹686.55 and a low of ₹680.85. Sellers held a slight edge, accounting for 52.80 per cent of total quantity against buyers at 47.20 per cent. Traded volume was a relatively subdued 42.75 lakh shares worth ₹292.18 crore, with deliverable quantity at 65.87 per cent, the highest this week.

The week’s dominant event remains Wednesday’s fresh 52-week low of ₹669.20, from which the stock has since partially recovered. The bank is down 31.12 per cent year-to-date, while the Nifty 50 has declined just 12.26 per cent over the same period. The P/E ratio compressed further to 13.16, with the adjusted figure at 12.97. Total market capitalisation stood at ₹10,53,328.67 crore.
The broader Bank Nifty provided some sector-level support, forming a second consecutive bullish candle and trading near 54,909, with resistance at 55,270–55,500 and support at 54,650–54,470.
HDFC Bank closes a turbulent week, marked by a leadership change, a fresh 52-week low, and persistent selling, with new MD & CEO Anup Bagchi yet to offer markets any strategic direction.

title: HDFC Bank drifts lower as week ends
